bug_semantics: In authenticated HTTP mode, an attacker-controlled Bearer token was treated as a session-file basename without restricting its alphabet or confining the resulting path. The token was joined as SESSION_DIR / f"{token}.session" and opened as a Telethon session. After the project added an exact-name denylist for the legacy session name `telegram`, a token such as `../fast-mcp-telegram/telegram` still resolved to the same default telegram.session file, passed the literal reserved-name comparison, and authenticated the remote client as that Telegram account.
flaw_origin: Commit 763b3e781d8fb0067fbedd85ea0f25d53a951a2e introduced multi-user HTTP Bearer authentication and the causal coupling between the raw header token and a filesystem path. Its src/server.py accepted any nonempty string after `Bearer ` and placed it in request context, while src/client/connection.py:38-55 created a client from SESSION_DIR / f"{token}.session" with no token-shape or path-containment check. Commit 1be7e62feb6160ecbe32d15f0ab940769f094968 later added exact reserved-name rejection but left that pre-existing path primitive unchanged, so it narrowed the direct `telegram` bypass without closing traversal aliases.
ai_marker: absent: `git cat-file -p 763b3e781d8fb0067fbedd85ea0f25d53a951a2e` shows human author and committer Alexey Leshchenko <leshchenko@gmail.com>; the BIC commit message has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, Made-with, AI-agent trailer, or bot identity.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/leshchenko1979/fast-mcp-telegram/security/advisories/GHSA-rxw2-pc8j-vxwm identifies the vulnerable range as <=0.19.0, patched in 0.19.1, and demonstrates that `../fast-mcp-telegram/telegram` reaches the documented default ~/.config/fast-mcp-telegram/telegram.session while the exact token `telegram` is denied.

`git blame -L 25,55 763b3e781d8fb0067fbedd85ea0f25d53a951a2e -- src/client/connection.py` assigns token generation, request-token context, `_get_client_by_token`, and especially line 51 `session_path = SESSION_DIR / f"{token}.session"` to the BIC. `git blame -L 55,125 ... -- src/server.py` assigns the HTTP Authorization extraction to the same BIC; lines 81-90 check only the `Bearer ` prefix/nonemptiness and return the raw token.

Immediate-parent verification: `git diff 4aa2ab04ee5b1da0be78173f98ac77ed91e0f282 763b3e781d8fb0067fbedd85ea0f25d53a951a2e -- src/client/connection.py src/server.py` shows the BIC adding the entire token context/authentication flow and raw token-derived session path. The parent tree has only a singleton `TelegramClient(SESSION_PATH, ...)`, no `_get_client_by_token`, no Bearer-token path construction, and no HTTP Bearer extraction. Thus the causal multi-user path traversal mechanism is absent from the immediate parent.

Lifecycle check: `git log -S'RESERVED_SESSION_NAMES' -- src/server_components/auth.py src/server.py` finds reserved-name protection added later in 1be7e62feb6160ecbe32d15f0ab940769f094968. Its diff adds only case-insensitive exact-name checks in auth.py and does not change src/client/connection.py, proving that the later guard did not introduce or repair the raw path join.

Version boundary: `git tag --points-at` maps the safe parent 4aa2ab04ee5b1da0be78173f98ac77ed91e0f282 to 0.1.4 and the BIC 763b3e781d8fb0067fbedd85ea0f25d53a951a2e to 0.2.0. `git merge-base --is-ancestor` confirms the BIC is an ancestor of advisory-listed vulnerable tag 0.19.0 (77bdf6d7e5c6a84d87acc423db613e6c6ba30094).

Fix and patched release: direct commit https://github.com/alexeyleshchenko/fast-mcp-telegram/commit/247637f49e364289c64332afe399c728de915811 adds strict 43-character URL-safe token validation plus resolved-path containment and routes verifier/connection/auth middleware through it. `git log --ancestry-path --reverse 167ab705f1cd09b21e85c370570471fe75a4f8c9..fabdeb06038318fbaa815b85c9a15b149b52233d` shows that direct fix as the second parent merged by fabdeb06038318fbaa815b85c9a15b149b52233d; tag 0.19.1 resolves exactly to that merge, and ancestry checks confirm the fix is included.
reasoning: The smallest causal BIC is the original multi-user authentication commit, not the March 2026 SessionFileTokenVerifier rewrite, the November 2025 reserved-name hardening, or the May 2026 fix. Before 763b3e781d8fb0067fbedd85ea0f25d53a951a2e, the immediate parent used one configured singleton session and had no attacker-selected Bearer token-to-path flow. The BIC simultaneously exposed a raw HTTP Bearer token and used it as a session filename, creating the traversal primitive. The later reserved-name commit made `telegram` fail literally but preserved the same path construction, allowing a traversal spelling to select the protected file; the later verifier copied the same flawed assumption rather than originating it. Release history brackets the lifecycle from 0.2.0 through 0.19.0, and the 0.19.1 merge contains the direct validation/containment fix. Finally, attribution is evaluated only on the BIC commit object: it records Alexey Leshchenko as both author and committer and contains no AI marker or trailer. AI attribution on the later fix is irrelevant, so the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
